subject: plyr: preserving (additional) attributes when splitting data.frames

messages.author: d5cb7ce4b6163739
messages.subject: plyr: preserving (additional) attributes when splitting data.frames
parts:
Dear all,

I create data.frames with additional attributes and would like to use
"dlply" in order to split the data.frames such that each piece
"inherits" the attributes. With plyr 1.7.1 this worked; now, with
version 1.8. it does not work anymore. Is it intended that plyr
"kills" additional attributes?

The following output illustrates the difference between versions 1.7.1
and 1.8.


# suppose the data.frame
> data = data.frame(x = c(1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2), y = rep(3, 6))

# suppose this data.frame has a the additional attribute
> attr(data, "test") <- 1

# shall be splitted according to x
> o <- dlply(data, .(x))
> o
$`1`
x y
1 1 3
2 1 3
3 1 3

$`2`
x y
1 2 3
2 2 3
3 2 3

# let's have a look at the attributes of the first list entry
# CASE 1) with plyr 1.7.1 (using R 2.14.1 on Windows 7, x86_32), we
get
> attributes(o[[1]])
$names
[1] "x" "y"

$test
[1] 1

$row.names
[1] 1 2 3

$class
[1] "data.frame"

$vars
[1] "x"

# CASE 2) with plyr 1.8 (using R 2.15.2 on Windows 7, x86_32), we get
the following

> attributes(o[[1]])
$names
[1] "x" "y"

$class
[1] "data.frame"

$row.names
[1] 1 2 3

$vars
[1] "x"


# PROBLEM: with plyr 1.8, the attribute "test" is lost



Thanks! Sincerely yours,
Tobias

messages.subject: Re: plyr: preserving (additional) attributes when splitting data.frames
parts:
Hmmm. It's not guaranteed to preserve them. If you file a bug report in GitHub I can take a look next time I'm working on plyr. 
Hadley
